chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Learns of a Ghost That Spreads by Word of Mouth
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang interrogates a terrified waiter and learns of a ghost that causes suoyang, a curse that spreads simply by being spoken about. A masterclass in informational horror.
og_title: A Ghost That Lives in Your Stories
og_description: How do you fight a curse that only exists because people talk about it? Li Huowang gets a terrifying lesson in viral folk horror.
twitter_title: The Scariest Ghost Can’t Be Seen
twitter_description: Li Huowang realizes the new enemy is not a demon, but information itself. A chilling chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A folk-medical and supernatural condition in Chinese culture where it is believed that male genitals can retract into the body, often attributed to spiritual attack or yin-energy imbalance.
The female equivalent of *suoyang*; a belief that female genitals can shrink or recede due to supernatural causes.
In Chinese folk religion, a ghost is the spirit of a deceased person, often a restless or unsatisfied one. They are usually invisible to the living and can cause misfortune.

A set of professional torture implements; in this context, Li Huowang uses it as a practical tool for intimidation rather than for genuine torture, as his psychological description alone breaks the subject.
A local administrative record of major events; an empty or sanitized gazetteer in the Dao-Twisted World signals official complicity or denial of supernatural horror.
